method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of a party to a civil proceeding, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; one rule module (the whole operative Act, each exported question calling a rule named by section) and one worked-case file; one regulative rule (s 6(5)(b)) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Jurisdiction of Courts (Cross-vesting) Act 1987 No 125 (NSW), act-1987-125, version of 2023-07-14 as collected by the Open Australian Legal Corpus (v7.1.0, NSW collected 2025-03-10), deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1987-125.txt (text sha256 c3c7c16b3c1876ca83a3ef4006321c0b763ff4b39d17787cc40281c5e4708f7a per its meta.json); unofficial and possibly out of date; no instrument brought in (none sets a number the Act uses)

seat: a party to a civil proceeding (s 3(1) party, including an intervener) whose case is in, or may be moved to or from, the Supreme Court of New South Wales

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run <file> for each of the two .l4 files, from this folder, one at a time
checks.result: 116 assertions written, 116 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in both files (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The whole operative Act. In: ss 3 (definitions used), 3A, 4(3)-(5), 5(1)-(4), (6)-(9), 6, 6A, 7, 8, 10, 11(1), (3), 12, 13, 14(2); s 9 as the premise of the transfer questions. Out: ss 1, 2, 15, 16 (machinery: name, commencement, reading down, suspension by proclamation); s 14(3) (a construction rule for other laws); s 6(5)(a) (the court's own adjournment power); the repealed provisions. Reasons in NOTES.md.
